src: Thought experiment about the Urge: What if it's a manifestation built and maintained by nano machines?||||Sounds far-fetched, right? But think about what other kind of technology is available to us nowadays and how that technology isn't really discernible or as a whole understandable anymore by most people because your average human doesn't have the technological expertise to understand the inner workings and individual parts of an object and how that object is constructed, how its parts are connected.||If you look at how the machines regulate and govern our lives it's at least not totally unrealistic to assume they might also take influence on us in other, more advanced technological ways.||||Note 1:||||This theory is crap. Stupid to assume the machines would try to finetune our motivations if they are in direct control of our bodies.||||Note 2:||||OK. What if it's not nano machines controlled by other machines or on their own, but a human controlling these nano machines and therefore influencing all of us?||||Note 3:||||( erased )

by Mortus||||There is no preordained meaning of life.||||But if you want your life to have a meaning you can have so, if you desire it. Chosen by yourself. Or, alternatively, you let others choose for you. But then it was a choice of your own to follow another person's design, and therefore this variant, too, inside the domain of your own volition.||||It's important to remember that every human is free from purpose, free from fate at the moment of birth, free from having to fulfill someone else's plan. We enter this world as free subjects of life, without carrying any initial mental burden.||||When we grow up we are of course shaped by the people around us and the experiences we make. Existence precedes essence, as the ancient Existentialists used to say. But at some point we begin to decide about our personal fate, our burden. We shape the mold inside the limitations of our individual life, inside the mental barriers and pre-configuration laid out by others, by the mentors we met on our way, and by the early experiences we made.||||We can pick our personal targets on that vast horizon. We can move around that chaotic structure of life so our path will find its way around obstacles, comes close to points of interest and hopefully grants us moments of significance.||||Whatever form the shape of our grand design takes, it will be pushed by an intrinsic force. This force is present, regardless of us wanting it or needing it. I call this the will, the unrelenting will that seems to inhabit any human. Unabated by any outside forces. The will not only to live but to live a fulfilled life. Create, travel, discover, experience. Maybe even act virtuously, as the will propels us to become a better and stronger version of ourselves.||||People under the spell of the unrelenting will are, at its most extreme version, even forceful enough to inspire other people.||||It might be a force, but the important point here is that I myself can choose where to direct it. Reflection about the unrelenting will strengthens our autonomy. This life doesn't have to be aimless.||||P.S.: Don't forget to take care of all that anxiety, coming as a ballast of being an autonomous human being.
Swimming through the dreams.||||Surfacing. Recognizing. Realizing.||||Put down the tools on the bank, and begin carving.||||All for science and ascension.

We put one of the rats in the tube. ||After exposing it to small amounts of refined ore it got highly agitated.||||We increased exposure, and started to see visible mutations. The fur began to fall off, and at even higher values the skin started to peel.||||A later dissection showed that the inner organs had combined into a single clump of flesh, which continued to pulsate for several hours even after removal from the rats body.||||Further experiments with even higher exposure should be conducted with utmost care.

I got the job.||||Whoever works for Cafière is taken care of for life, they say.||Who says this? I don't know. It's just a thing they say.||||I actually met Cafière once. He's nice. Offered to give me a better bed when I was talking about my back pains.||I declined. I'd rather go out and try to meet somebody.||When I said that, Cafière laughed. Then he started looking worried.||Couldn't help me with that, he said.

They shot Vulko yesterday.||||I don't know how they knew he was trying to sneak out info about the experiments. ||I didn't even know he was trying to get out.||||These robots, quietly tuckering around day and night. Apparently they follow our orders, but nobody dares to even approach them.

I had a lot of nightmares recently. And apparently so do the others. ||||We talked about it during the break. They seem connected.||We all see clumps of amorphous flesh waltzing around. Prying open our heads. Staring at us.||||How can this be? Is it that our work somehow connected our psyches?||What a preposterous hypothesis. It has to be something else.||||Yet, even though we are haunted by these fleshy images, our craving for a good steak for lunch is not going down.

Why the fuck would this place need a head officer?||||The guys are working on their own. I don't even know what their work is about.||But no-oh. Cafière wants to have somebody here. Fill the seat in their absence.||||At least the pay is good. It would be better if I could actually leave and go to a place where I can spend that money.||||Being indoors all the time is starting to impact my vision. My head hurts all the time.||I shouted at one of those damn metal things to go and get me something to better my eyes. ||I don't think he understood. But shouting is fun. Might try that again.

I studied. As an engineer. Worked hard for my degree. Earned it. Barely passed, but I got it fair and square.||||And what Job do I get? Facility management?||I mean, I earn a lot better than I expected if I got something in my field.||And it's quite cushy. The bots take care of almost everything.||But still... were the last 10 years of my life wasted? Couldn't be.||||I still got that itch. I'm going to take a look at these machines tonight. There's got to be something I can improve with my knowledge. Even with those geniusses downstairs.
